raw_response:
I have only 6 mu, so I cannot afford to gamble. Since this land is in the wheat-maize rotation and I have well irrigation, I will keep the full 6 mu in winter wheat followed by summer maize. With my education, I do pay attention to rates and timing, but in the end I still farm for stability, not for some perfect number on paper. Wheat is the safer crop here in our system, so I will make sure the base fertilizer is adequate and keep one topdress option open depending on how the stand looks after winter. For maize, the turnaround after wheat harvest is very tight, so I will not do anything complicated. I will harvest wheat, do quick residue handling and shallow tillage, and plant maize immediately. Because groundwater irrigation costs money, I will irrigate by crop stage, not excessively. If rainfall is decent, I can save one irrigation; if it turns dry, I will protect the crop at the key stages first. I would rather keep a modest cash reserve than push input use too high on only 6 mu.
